item.title: Warriors star Stephen Curry leads Golden State to dominant OT win over Magic
item.description: Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Warriors star Stephen Curry leads Golden State to dominant OT win over Magic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors just keep finding ways to win. The Warriors outlasted the Orlando Magic 126-119 in overtime on Saturday night at Chase Center, as Curry delivered yet another vintage performance to extend the team’s winning streak to seven games . The two-time MVP was simply unstoppable , finishing with 41 points on a blistering 13-of-19 shooting from the field. He knocked down five of his 10 3-point attempts and went a perfect 10-of-10 from the free-throw line, while also adding six rebounds and six assists. The performance also put Curry in the record books . He now has the most 40-point games by a player 35 years or older in NBA history. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The superstar guard came through when the Warriors needed him most. With Golden State clinging to a 120-118 lead in the final minute of overtime, Curry was still going at the Magic defense, having already reached the 41-point mark, as Golden State pulled away for the win. It was the latest in a string of big nights for Curry during the streak. He dropped 34 points against the Phoenix Suns last Monday and followed that up with 29 points in just 28 minutes in Thursday’s blowout win over the Miami Heat . Curry had plenty of help against Orlando, too. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg continued his impressive start with 23 points on 9-of-15 shooting, along with eight rebounds and three blocks. Brandin Podziemski chipped in 15 points and seven rebounds, knocking down four of his five 3-point attempts, while Draymond Green orchestrated the offense with 13 assists. As a team, the Warriors shot 53.8% from the field and 46.9% from deep, and they dished out 32 assists. The Magic made the Warriors work for it. Franz Wagner led Orlando with 30 points and 11 assists, while Wendell Carter Jr. posted 19 points and 11 rebounds . Tristan da Silva added 19 points, and Anthony Black and Jamal Cain each scored 18. Orlando also dominated the offensive glass with 24 offensive rebounds, but its 38.1% shooting from the field proved costly. The win improved Golden State to 7-3 on the season, a remarkable turnaround after the team opened the year with three straight losses . Since then, the Warriors have not lost a game. Curry and the Warriors will look to make it eight in a row when they close out their homestand against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday. item.title: Steph Curry rides to the rescue, propels Warriors to seventh straight win
item.description: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry, celebrating during the first half of Saturday's game against the Orlando Magic at Chase Center, scored 41 points. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) Stephen Curry removed the towel draped over his head, dropped the ice pack attached to his right knee and climbed off his chair to return to the court. The Golden State Warriors didn't need Curry to close some games during their early-season winning streak. They needed him this time. Twice. Curry scored 12 points in the final four-plus minutes of regulation Saturday night at Chase Center, nearly ushering the Warriors to victory. But Orlando's Jamal Cain corralled an offensive rebound and scored with 1.5 seconds left, pushing the game into overtime. Curry and Draymond Green both stayed on the bench to start OT, a nod to their advanced basketball age and the effort they expended all night. They rested briefly, then returned to the court - and Curry added five more points as the Warriors earned a 126-119 victory over the pesky Magic. Curry finished with 41 points - his 16th game of 40 or more points since he turned 35, extending his NBA record - as Golden State (7-3) won its seventh consecutive game, its longest streak since March 2025. Yaxel Lendeborg added 23 points, Brandin Podziemski scored 15 and Green dished out 13 assists. Franz Wagner led Orlando with 30 points. This was Curry's second game this season with 40-plus points. He also scored 44 in an Oct. 28 road win over Minnesota. The Warriors won despite 18 turnovers. They also struggled on the boards: Orlando outrebounded them 57-42. Curry returned with 4:34 left in regulation and the game tied at 96. He promptly channeled his 28-year-old self - remember, he's actually 38 - and scored on an array of long-range shots, feathery floaters and driving layups. In all, Curry went 13-for-19 from the field, including 5-for-10 from long distance. After making a habit of digging early holes in recent games - and then storming back to win - the Warriors jumped ahead Wednesday. They seemed on the verge of blowing out short-handed Orlando, only to see a 16-point halftime lead evaporate in a ragged third quarter. The Magic took their first lead of the game at the 3:23 mark of the quarter, when Tristan da Silva buried a 3-pointer. That seemed to stun both the Warriors and the crowd. Golden State had built its cushion by moving the ball crisply in the first half, repeatedly leading to open shots. The Warriors finished the half with 19 assists on 22 made shots from the field. item.description: West's final playoff spots, East craziness & more from Decision Day By Charles Boehm However your club may have fared on the pitch, Decision Day remains undefeated. The 2026 MLS regular season ended with a bang on Saturday, with twists and turns right down to the final minutes in both the Eastern and Western Conference. Out West, three teams stepped up to grab their places in the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs, while three others tasted bitter disappointment as their chances slipped away. The Eastern Conference’s drama centered on seeding, with some late surprises benefiting arguably the hottest team in the league, and others raising troubling questions, even for world-renowned icons. Now everyone can catch their breath as the November FIFA international window unfolds. Pulses then get racing again in less than two weeks, when the Wild Card round kicks off MLS’s most exciting month, culminating in the 2026 MLS Cup presented by Audi final on Dec. 18. Let’s dive into how Decision Day unfolded and where it leads us next. ⚽ 🏆 Think You’ve Got the Winning Bracket?! The Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs Bracket Challenge is now open. Make your picks, build your bracket, and compete for your chance to win. Play Now Real Salt Lake RSL in, Galaxy out The day’s six-pointer of all six-pointers unfolded in Sandy, Utah, where Real Salt Lake and the LA Galaxy faced off, both essentially needing a win to book their playoff spot. Alas, the Galaxy didn’t show up early, falling behind 2-0 before 15 minutes had elapsed and never really grasping the magnitude of the moment. Zach Booth sure did, though: A Luc de Fougerolles own goal kept things tense right up until the final whistle. But RSL held on for a 2-1 win that sends them into the postseason for the fifth straight year, the longest such streak in the Western Conference. item.title: LSU’s Lane Kiffin Places Blame for Brutal Loss Against Alabama
item.description: AUBURN, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 24: Head coach Lane Kiffin of the LSU Tigers looks on during the first half of an NCAA football game against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan Hare Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Auburn, Alabama. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) Getty On a Saturday with plenty of separation in college football, the No. 14 LSU Tigers had an opportunity to earn a massive win over the No. 5 Alabama Crimson Tide in front of their home crowd at Tiger Stadium. Yet, despite recording 14 more first downs than the Crimson Tide and nearly 200 more total yards offensively, LSU lost 31-13. The Tigers turned the ball over twice and went 0-for-4 on fourth-down conversions, which ultimately proved costly. Lane Kiffin Places Blame for Loss When breaking down why LSU failed to get the job done despite statistically outplaying Alabama in several categories, Kiffin pointed to the Tigers’ struggles in the red zone and on fourth down. “It was a very unusual statistical game, you know, yardage wise 457 to 285 and comes down to red zone and fourth downs,” Kiffin said. “We didn’t make any. 0-for-4 on fourth downs and we got in the red zone more than they did. That’ll give you a problem on the scoreboard when you have a lot of yards and that happens.” Kiffin also gave Alabama credit for the way the Crimson Tide played. “Also I credit them. They did a really good job. Some good stuff with the blitz zero in the red zone and you know disguising it and had some good pick/rub plays that the guys got open and scored some touchdowns.” Lane Kiffin on LSU’s loss to Alabama: “It comes down to red zone and 4th downs. We didn’t make any, 0/4 on 4th downs, and we got in the red zone more than they did.” “They had some good pick/rub plays that the guys got open and scored some touchdowns.” https://t.co/XbrC2ReYdv — The Next Round (@NextRoundLive) November 8, 2026 Looking at LSU The Tigers are now 6-3 overall, which means their margin for error is nonexistent. They’ll need to win out, and even that might not be enough to get them into the College Football Playoff. However, LSU will certainly have opportunities to put together some strong wins down the stretch. The Tigers will face No. 7 Texas next week before wrapping up their season with matchups against No. 13 Tennessee and Arkansas. item.title: Postgame Reaction: Mackenzie Blackwood Gives Avalanche a Chance to Find Their Game vs Detroit
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There’s an alternate universe where Mackenzie Blackwood doesn’t stand on his head in the first period Saturday. While the rest of the Colorado Avalanche struggled through a flat opening 20 minutes, their goalie made 13 saves and kept the visiting Detroit Red Wings off the board. The Avs came out stronger in the second period and made good use of their goalie’s early work. They scored twice on four power plays in the middle frame alone and added two more goals in the third (one more on the PP) on their way to a 4-0 victory over the Red Wings at Ball Arena. Blackwood covered for them early and was eventually rewarded with his first shutout of the season. He made 14 additional saves over the final 40 minutes to finish with 27. “It’s nice to be rewarded,” Blackwood said. “I mean, I thought I’ve been kind of stringing some good games together. Obviously, they’re going to score goals in the NHL most nights, but whenever you can come away with zero, it’s a good feeling.” Colorado’s top guys took over from there. Martin Necas had two goals and two assists, while Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar each added a goal and two helpers. All three scored on the power play, which finished 3-for-5 after failing to capitalize on its first two opportunities. “I think special teams and these little things, they get us going,” Necas said. “You need a little help for the power play, and then you know it brings the momentum on your side.” This season has featured plenty of hot and cold stretches for Colorado. Some nights, head coach Jared Bednar’s club looks like the same dominant team that won the Presidents’ Trophy last year. Other nights, it looks nothing like it. But it would be unfair to lump Blackwood into that conversation. He’s been one of the team’s consistent bright spots this season, even after a couple of rough outings early in the year. Blackwood improved to 9-3-1 on the season, and his save percentage climbed above .900 for the first time all year. He’s now been above that mark in seven of his last nine starts. Saturday’s first period was another example of why Colorado needs him to keep that pace. His performance ensured the Avalanche didn’t have to chase the game from behind, something that’s become all too common in recent weeks. “The first goal is so important in this league,” Bednar said. “I mean, check the stats on any team. item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results, kick-off times and how to watch
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship bursts back into life as the inaugural edition comes to a conclusion in a busy November. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. France and South Africa currently top the two pools, with New Zealand also unbeaten and level on points with the Springboks. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how it will all work: What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. The 1st vs 1st match is worth two points, with all other matches in the finals weekend worth one. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom will be able to watch every game on ITV after the free-to-air broadcaster struck a deal to show the competition. item.title: SEC football power rankings after separation Saturday in Week 10
item.description: All 16 SEC teams played in Week 10. All of the top eight teams in the standings played against each other. Most notably, the Georgia Bulldogs thumped the Ole Miss Rebels 42-7 on the road. Georgia looks like the best team in the country while Ole Miss' College Football Playoff hopes suffered a major blow. Georgia is the top team in our power rankings. After Georgia in our power rankings is the Texas Longhorns , who earned a big 34-20 road win over the Missouri Tigers in a game that featured two teams with playoff aspirations. Missouri goes on the road to play Georgia next week. The Tennessee Volunteers delivered at home and beat the Kentucky Wildcats 34-6. Kentucky was actually tied with Georgia atop the SEC standings entering Week 10. However, the Wildcats did not look like an SEC championship contender against Tennessee, who has gone under the radar. The Alabama Crimson Tide continue to have a perfect record against coach Lane Kiffin. Alabama used a strong performance from its defense to dispatch LSU in a big road win for the Crimson Tide. Alabama's red zone defense looked particularly strong. The Crimson Tide justified their loft No. 5 ranking. Alabama, Kentucky, Tennessee and Texas all have two losses in conference play while Georgia has just one. Every other SEC team has at least three losses. Georgia is looking like a lock to make the SEC championship, while the Bulldogs' most likely opponent is up in the air with Alabama having a good chance to advance. Oklahoma notched a 23-7 road win over Florida, who suddenly is having offensive woes (although Florida has played two great defenses over the past two weeks). Vanderbilt beat Mississippi State 25-23 in a battle of two of the SEC's worst teams. Auburn beat Arkansas 26-23 in another less notable SEC contest. item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce (87) walks off the field after a loss against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. © Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Rob Gronkowski’s red-jacket day in Foxborough belonged to one tight end, but a comparison from a former teammate pulled another one into the conversation. Gronkowski became the 38th member of the Patriots Hall of Fame on Saturday. The same day, former Patriots linebacker Rob Ninkovich compared him with Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, in a comparison that left many fans asking why Kelce was the topic of conversation on such a big night for Gronkowski. 2-Time Patriots Champ Takes a Shot At Travis Kelce Ninkovich, one of the former teammates who took part in the ceremony, kept his tribute simple. “Like everyone up here said, it made everybody better to have Rob on the field. Practices were harder than the games. So, thank you, congratulations. We love you.” He then measured Gronkowski against Kelce: “[Travis] Kelce and [Rob Gronkowski] don’t even come close. He’s a receiver, and this guy is a tight end.” One fan went straight at the second half of Ninkovich’s line. “If your argument against a tight end is that he’s too good at receiving, I think we found the problem with your argument.” Others pointed to the timing, since the comparison came on a day built around Gronkowski. “The fact that Kelce is getting mentioned at Gronk’s HoF induction kinda disproves Rob’s point,” a fan wrote. Gronkowski, who beat Adam Vinatieri and Logan Mankins in the fan vote, didn’t hide what the day meant to him. “This honor today means everything to me. item.title: Justin Allgaier praised for his impact as leader and mentor in NASCAR O'Reilly garage
item.description: Motorsport photo Justin Allgaier is now a two-time NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series champion , and while he will get plenty of accolades for his on-track success, the driver of the No. 7 JR Motorsports Chevrolet is also a guiding force for the young drivers he is consistently beating for these race wins and now two championships. The ages of the four drivers Allgaier bested on Saturday are 20, 21, 23, and 29. He also has three full-time teammates under the age of 25, making the 40-year-old Allgaier a valuable asset as a mentor for to his teammates at JR Motorsports. Allgaier seems like the bar these rising stars look to to make themselves better drivers both behind the wheel and beyond the track. He is also the one on the receiving end of many of the mistakes as they improve their craft on the track. Allgaier's unique position among the NOAPS garage Justin Allgaier and Jesse Love talk after race Justin Allgaier and Jesse Love talk after race Motorsport.com asked team owner Dale Earnhardt Jr. about Allgaier's unique role in the garage, acknowledging it must be difficult at times to be a mentor when you're also the driver paying the price for many of their mistakes. "We all hear it," said Earnhardt. "Justin mentors drivers that aren’t even on our team. He has to put up with so much crap. All these young guys come to this series, make so many mistakes around him, he has to kind of bite his tongue so many times. Even in our own building, we’ve had races where we get these young guys that come in, you’re trying to shepherd them, tutor them, create an opportunity for them. "The idea in a perfect world is they’re there for a short period of time, then move up. They knock Justin out of the way somewhere. You got to figure out how to have that conversation with them and where they learn a lesson, but also get Justin to understand his role as a veteran within the team, ’cause he’s the constant. item.title: Karl-Anthony Towns Gets Real About His Humbling NBA Journey: ‘Stop Trying To Prove Yourself To Everyone’
item.description: CLEVELAND, OH - NOVEMBER 7: Karl-Anthony Towns #32 of the New York Knicks shoots a free throw during the game against the Cleveland Cavaliers on November 7, 2026 at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/NBAE via Getty Images) Karl-Anthony Towns and the New York Knicks defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 109-97 tonight, led by a monster performance from the 30-year-old center. He finished with 29 points, 13 rebounds, three assists, and two blocks, shooting 11-21 from the field (52.4% FG) and 2-4 from beyond the arc (50.0% 3P). After the win, Karl-Anthony Towns spoke to Mike Breen and Clyde Frazier, who asked him about the key to rebounding and at what point in his career he stopped caring about scoring every night and instead shifted his focus to doing what it takes to win, which tonight meant dominating on the boards. “It’s a sexy stat to me that damn sure looks sexy to me,” Towns said initially. “Rebounding for me, it comes from my father. My father always told me that if you don’t give opponents a second chance at a shot, and you’re an offensive player who gets that second shot, it’s like a two-for-one special; you see the rim, and it feels like it gets bigger.” “You shoot the ball with a lot more confidence when you get the second chance. Being able to make sure that our team doesn’t give them any second chances and also, for us on offense, giving my teammates the confidence that they can shoot with confidence and know that whatever happens, I’m going to be right next to the rim getting us the rebound and a second chance at it.” “Rebounding, to me, is about establishing the confidence of this team to shoot the ball with full confidence and allowing them to understand that, regardless of the result, if you take care of the process and do your best with your jumper or your finishing, your teammate has your back,” Karl-Anthony Towns further explained. item.description: Denver's Nikola Jokic and Indiana's Ivica Zubac battle for the ball in the Nuggets' NBA victory over the Pacers in Mexico City (Alfredo ESTRELLA) Jalen Brunson scored 31 points to propel the NBA champion New York Knicks to a convincing 109-97 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Saturday in a rematch of last season's Eastern Conference finals. Brunson scored 18 points in the second quarter as the Knicks broke open a close game in Cleveland, where the Cavs were coming off an impressive win over LeBron James and the Eastern Conference-leading Philadelphia 76ers on Friday. The NBA Finals Most Valuable Player added six rebounds and nine assists. Karl-Anthony Towns had 29 points with 13 rebounds and two steals for the Knicks, who notched their fifth win in six games after starting the season 0-3. Donovan Mitchell scored 37 points to lead the Cavs, but Cleveland felt the absence of center Jarrett Allen and when Brunson took over in the second period they couldn't respond. The Knicks pushed the lead to as many as 19 points. They connected on just 42.7% of their shots from the field but came up with 26 second-chance points off 16 offensive rebounds. "Ugly game, but just a good win by our guys," Knicks coach Mike Brown said. "We did enough to get it done in some way, shape or form. Anytime you can get a win, especially with us starting out 0-3, we'll take it to see if we can build a little positive equity at this point in the season." In San Francisco, Stephen Curry scored 19 of his 41 points in the fourth quarter and overtime to help the Golden State Warriors escape with a 126-119 victory over the Orlando Magic. Golden State led by as many as 16, but with the help of 19 Warriors turnovers the Magic clawed back and a frantic fourth quarter saw Orlando's Jamal Cain tie it with 1.5 seconds left in regulation. Curry converted a three-point play with 1:38 left in the extra session that put Golden State up by two and added a layup with less than a minute remaining to help the Warriors hang on for a seventh straight win. Curry, 38, posted his second 40-point game this season and passed LeBron James for most 40-point games after the age of 35 with his 16th. - Mexico City Game - Saturday's seven-game slate started with the NBA's latest foray south of the border for its 16th regular-season contest in Mexico. Three-time MVP Nikola Jokic scored 19 points and grabbed 13 rebounds to help the Denver Nuggets hold off the Indiana Pacers' second-half surge and emerge with a 114-102 triumph. Jokic added eight assists, coming up just shy of a triple-double. Cameron Johnson added 18 points and Jamal Murray chipped in 16 for the Nuggets, who saw a 27-point lead sliced to seven midway through the fourth quarter but held on for the victory before a sellout crowd of more than 20,000 at Mexico City's Arena CDMX. "It was a good crowd," Jokic said. "The energy was there the whole game. I didn't know who they were cheering for, for us or for them, but the energy was there." India

item.title: Recap: Avalanche put Red Wings on Ice with 4-0 shutout
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 07: Martin Necas #88 of the Colorado Avalanche scores a goal during the second period of the game against the Detroit Red Wings at Ball Arena on November 07, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Maclean/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images Before embarking on quite an important road trip, the Colorado Avalanche had one last matter to take care of at home. The task at hand was hosting the Detroit Red Wings in the debut of Colorado’s very blue Hometown Remix threads. The home team gave their fans something to cheer about in the 4-0 victory, Colorado’s first shutout of the season. Mackenzie Blackwood made 27 saves and Martin Nečas scored a pair of goals as the Avalanche cruised to their 10th win. The Game It was a slow start in the first period, which has become all too common, but at least the Avalanche didn’t give up a goal. Still, they were outshot 13-5 despite some back and forth action. Neither team committed a penalty either, so there would (definitely) be opportunity later. As suspected, the second period featured a healthy amount of special teams time and on their third power play, the Avalanche finally got on the board. Martin Nečas found a loose puck on the doorstep and was able to sweep it past Detroit goaltender Danil Tarasov. Colorado scored another power play goal minutes later, as the Detroit penalty killers were clearly tired, and Nathan MacKinnon put one home from his favorite spot to put Colorado up by two after two. Colorado extended their lead early in the third period as Nečas got his second goal of the night with some nifty hand-eye coordination as he swatted the puck behind Tarasov. Then, Gabe Landeskog and Moritz Seider had a surprisingly spirited tilt, which led to another Avalanche power play in which Cale Makar finally found the back of the net for his first power play goal on the season. Up 4-0 the game was all but over and it finally was as Mackenzie Blackwood secured a 27-save shutout for the win. GABRIEL LANDESKOG AND MORITZ SEIDER DROPPED THE GLOVES 😱👊 pic.twitter.com/WzQzLcEfHi — Gino Hard (@GinoHard_) November 8, 2026 Takeaways Not sure the game needed an AHL level of 14 penalties, specially since none were taken in the first period, but with five power plays and Detroit’s 25th ranked penalty kill, it all helped get the Avalanche out of a funk. Their special teams made the difference tonight, which is something the team needed and can hopefully build off of. Cale Makar played just under 23 minutes in this game even with six minutes of power play time. Reducing the load on him might be the new tactic to rejuvenate the superstar defenseman and get him back to creating dynamic offense every night. And early returns with one goal on the evening might encourage the coaching staff to keep the strategy going. item.title: 5 things we learned from Ohio State football's loss to Oregon
item.description: Here are five things we learned from No. 12 Ohio State’s 41-28 loss to No. 23 Oregon on Nov. 7: The CFP path is nearly shut The bubble likely burst for the Buckeyes. The unraveling against the Ducks leaves Ohio State with a remote chance of reaching the College Football Playoff. No one with three regular-season losses has ever made the playoff, and the Buckeyes were already out of the field when the selection committee revealed its first set of rankings earlier in the week. The Buckeyes are not mathematically eliminated from making the Big Ten championship game. With two conference losses, they could get help over the last three weeks of the regular season in order to reach Indianapolis and vie for the league’s automatic bid. But the nature of their second straight loss, one in which they surrendered a double-digit lead and allowed 38 consecutive points, makes the prospect of an at-large berth rather improbable. The Buckeyes have a range of issues that extend beyond the loss of starting quarterback Julian Sayin to injury, and it’s likely they will plunge to the bottom of the committee’s next rankings if not fall out entirely. Unless they snap back over the coming weeks and things break their way at the top of the Big Ten standings, the Buckeyes look like they’re poised to become the second straight preseason No. 1 team to miss the playoff entirely. Defense hasn’t risen to the occasion Ohio State’s defense needed to step up following the loss of Sayin. It’s instead fallen apart, bearing significant responsibility for two straight loss losses to Oregon and USC. The Buckeyes have allowed 71 points in a span of two weeks, surrendering at least 30 points in consecutive games during the regular season for the first time since 2021. They were again vulnerable to big plays. After not giving up a play from scrimmage of 40 or more yards through seven games, they have allowed three in two weeks. Running back Dierre Hill Jr. broke loose for a 48-yard touchdown run in the third quarter after he dodged an attempt at a shoestring tackle by linebacker Christian Alliegro and outran other defensive backs. The Buckeyes allowed the Ducks to convert four times on third down when they needed at least 10 yards to move the chains. The pass rush did little to impact quarterback Dylan Raiola, who was never sacked and hurried only twice. There were missed opportunities for game-changing plays as well.
